newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Siemens CEO says Transrapid still alive.
newsitem.headline: Siemens CEO says Transrapid still alive.

text.p: Siemens AG chief Heinrich von Pierer said on Friday Germany's proposed Transrapid high-speed railway project still had a chance to secure financing and government approval in 1997.
"The Transrapid still has a chance. The decision will come this year," Pierer told Reuters at the World Economic Forum.
"Foreign investors have been contacted. There is interest from the foreign side in taking part in the project."
Foreign participation must be explored, Pierer said.

The project's fate depends on economic studies due in the first half of 1997. The studies would look at potential ticket prices, passenger numbers and the cost of the Berlin-to-Hamburg magnetic levitation line.
"The Transrapid must be economically feasible, and it must have broad political support," he said.
Siemens' partners in the Trnasrapid consortium include Thyssen AG, Bilfinger & Berger, Hocktief and Holzmann.
